interpretationText.deathsBeforeObjective: The group reached the objective at a numbers disadvantage: that is an unfavourable situation, not proof of an individual mistake.
interpretationText.objectiveLostAfterFight: The death happened in a fight the group was already losing; the objective conversion follows it, not necessarily because of it.
interpretationText.killsWithoutConversion: A kill advantage that became neither a structure nor an objective: time gained that was not converted.
interpretationText.leadFading: A lead disappearing is a sign of the game, not of one person: it is worth reviewing what the group stopped converting in that stretch.
interpretationText.teamSplit: Proximity is not coordination: the number shows they were far apart, not that the distance caused the loss.
interpretationText.objectiveOutnumbered: Contesting at a numbers disadvantage: the call to contest is the team's, and so is the cost.
interpretationText.deathsIntoStructures: Chain deaths take away the group's chance to defend: the structure falls in the stretch when people were missing.
interpretationText.noInflection: The result came from accumulation over the game, not from a single episode — or this match's data does not allow isolating one.

impactText.none: It was not possible to isolate a moment when the state of the game changed measurably.
impactText.measured: {direction, select, gain {Gain} loss {Loss} other {Change}} of {gold} gold in the stretch ({before} → {after}), {sign}{objectives} objective(s) for the group.

improvementText.deathsBeforeObjective: Back off 60s before the objective when people are missing: arriving late is worse than not contesting.
improvementText.objectiveLostAfterFight: After a lost fight, decide as a group whether the objective is still worth it — and leave together when it is not.
improvementText.killsWithoutConversion: After winning a fight, call the next action (turret, dragon) before going back to lane.
improvementText.leadFading: When ahead, reduce risk: trade hunting for map pressure and objective vision.
improvementText.teamSplit: Agree on the meeting point before contesting: someone always arrives last.
improvementText.objectiveOutnumbered: Do not start or contest an objective with fewer people than needed; call the count first.
improvementText.deathsIntoStructures: After the second death in a row, play safe until the team is back: the structure falls in the meantime.
improvementText.noInflection: Reviewing the whole match instead of one stretch helps more here: the analysis found no decisive episode.

notEvaluatedText.noVision: Vision (wards) is not collected: vision control before objectives cannot be measured.
notEvaluatedText.sampledTimeline: The timeline is sampled per minute, so two events within the same minute have no exact order.
notEvaluatedText.fewRosterPlayers: Few roster members in the match: group movement and spread were not evaluated.
notEvaluatedText.noObjectives: The timeline recorded no group objectives in this match: conversion was not evaluated.

patterns.emptyHint: Recurring patterns need matches with a timeline to show up.

patterns.limitations: What this pattern does not prove
patterns.deathsHint: Mean, median and dispersion of the group's deaths in each match of the recent window.

unpreparedObjectives.title: Objective contested without enough people
unpreparedObjectives.behavior: The group contests dragon or baron with fewer than {players} people nearby instead of waiting for the team to group up.

limitations.sampling: Proximity is measured in map units over a sample of about one frame per minute: someone on the way may look absent.
limitations.position: Position shows where the player was, not whether they decided or were kept from being there.

deathsBeforeObjectives.title: Deaths shortly before the objective
deathsBeforeObjectives.behavior: The group loses people in the {seconds}s before dragon or baron and reaches the objective at a numbers disadvantage.

limitations.cause: A death before the objective can be the cause of the disadvantage or the effect of a fight already lost.
limitations.window: The {seconds}s window is a convention: objectives contested earlier do not count.

killsWithoutConversion.title: Kill clusters without an objective after them
killsWithoutConversion.behavior: The group gets two or more kills in a short window and captures no objective right after, going back to lane instead of pressing the numbers advantage.

limitations.notEveryCluster: Not every cluster offers an objective: a kill while the dragon is not up is not a conversion mistake.
limitations.availability: Objective availability is not measured here — only whether a capture happened in the window.

killsWithoutConversion.note: {unconverted} of {clusters} kill clusters without an objective

leadNotConverted.title: Gold lead that did not become a win
leadNotConverted.behavior: The group opens a gold lead and does not turn it into enough structures to close the game.

limitations.notAlwaysError: Leading in gold and losing is not always a conversion mistake: a scaling composition can lose while ahead.
limitations.peakGold: The lead is measured by peak gold, which may have come from a single fight late in the game.

isolatedDeaths.title: Deaths with no ally nearby
isolatedDeaths.behavior: The group allows deaths of someone far from any ally, the kind of death that comes from being away from the team rather than from a bad collective call.

limitations.farIsNotWrong: Being far does not mean being wrong: on a split push or defending a lane, the distance is the plan.
limitations.sampling: The position sample is about one frame per minute, so the approach may not show up.

isolatedDeaths.note: {share}% of deaths without an ally nearby

collapseGames.title: Matches far below their own standard
collapseGames.behavior: The group has games where it dies far above its usual rate: the sign of a match that fell apart, not of a longer game.

limitations.duration: A 35-minute game naturally has more deaths than a 20-minute one: part of the difference is duration, not a drop in level.
limitations.smallSample: With few matches the group's reference is unstable and the cut-off is imprecise.

reason.deathsTeamPace: The whole group dies at the same pace: the evidence separates the person from the pattern and points at the collective.
reason.deathsNoTimeline: Deaths are high, but without a timeline there is no telling whether they were isolated or in a fight.
reason.deathsWithAllies: Most deaths happened with allies nearby ({share}% alone): the team fight explains more than the individual decision.
reason.kpNoTimeline: Without a timeline, there is no telling whether the person stayed out of fights or the fights happened far from them.
reason.combatLaneBehind: A laning phase behind in XP explains much of the low damage: it is the lane's problem, not the fight's.

exercise.farmingUnstableRole: Treat as a lineup theme: settle the person's role before reading the farm.
exercise.farmingProblem: Review the first 10 minutes of the matches, especially wave management after the recall.
exercise.farmingStrength: Keep the recall routine that is working and share it with the rest of the lane.
exercise.visionProblem: Place a ward before each objective in the next 4 matches and count how many were contested.
exercise.visionStrength: Document where the wards are being placed: that is the positioning to teach the team.
exercise.deathsTeamPace: Treat as a team theme: agree on what to do after the second death in a row before pointing at a player.
exercise.deathsNoTimeline: Collect the timeline of the next matches to tell an isolated death from a team-fight death.
exercise.deathsWithAllies: Review the team fights: entry, target order and exit.
exercise.deathsProblem: Before walking into the jungle alone, check where the two closest allies are.
exercise.kpNoTimeline: Collect the timeline of the next matches before asking for fight presence.
exercise.kpProblem: Over the next 5 matches, follow the team between 12 and 20 minutes instead of staying in the lane.
exercise.kpStrength: Keep the fight presence and call the lane to the objectives that happen after them.
exercise.combatLaneBehind: Review the plan for the first 10 minutes before asking for fight efficiency.
exercise.combatProblem: In review, look at the fights where the person died first: pick a target before going in and leave alive.
exercise.combatStrength: Use the fights where the trades went well as a reference: position and target before contact.

lineup.title: Lineup
lineup.readOnly: Read-only page. Whoever has the link sees the lineup.
lineup.incompleteGames: {count, plural, one {# game} other {# games}} without 5

dimensions.title: Team dimensions
dimensions.subtitle: Recent window: {recent} games ({recentFull} with 5 people) · previous window: {previous} games ({previousFull} with 5). No single score: every number brings its sample.
dimensions.caveat: Every metric is independent and carries its own n. "Change" is (after − before) compared to the standard error of the difference (Welch t), not to the games' spread: "within noise" means the 95% interval of the change contains zero. Nothing here is causal.
dimensions.empty: Not enough data for the dimensions yet.

metrics.dragonPresence: Dragon with 3+ of the team nearby
metrics.deathsBeforeObjective: Team deaths in the 60s before an objective
metrics.groupedShare: Moments with the whole team together
metrics.killParticipationGap: Gap between the highest and lowest kill participation

gold.title: Gold per minute
gold.hint: The team's gold difference, minute by minute, over {games} games with a timeline ({missing} missing). The light line is the median, the band is the interquartile range and the colours split wins from losses.
gold.aria: Team gold difference per minute: median, interquartile band, wins and losses.
gold.axes: Vertical axis: gold difference (above zero = team ahead, below = behind), capped at {limit}. Horizontal axis: minutes of the match.
gold.caveat: Only games whose last frame reached the minute enter; the sample shrinks at the end. "Ahead" = +1k or more; "behind" = −1k or less. Association with the win, never a cause.

synergy.title: Observed pair synergy
synergy.hint: Games where both took part in the same kill, against what their individual kill participation predicts (0.70 × 0.60 = 42%). A factor above 1× means more joint plays than expected. Minimum of {games} shared games ({unranked} pair(s) left out).
synergy.empty: Not enough games with a timeline for a pair yet ({games} needed).
synergy.caveat: Presence in a kill is a timeline record. It does not mean combination, communication or target focus.

insights.title: What the data shows
insights.subtitle: Every observation carries its number, its sample, its limitation and a suggested exercise. Nothing here is causal.

objectivePresenceHelps.title: Being at the objective with the team shows up in wins
objectivePresenceHelps.body: When 4 or more of the team were seen near an objective, wins: {withIt}. With nobody near: {withoutIt}.
objectivePresenceHelps.limitation: An association between presence and winning, not a cause. A game already won also gathers the team at objectives.
objectivePresenceHelps.exercise: Before starting dragon, check who is in the count: whoever is in the opposite lane pushes the wave first.

objectivePresenceWeak.title: Presence at the objective is not showing up in wins
objectivePresenceWeak.body: When the team was near an objective, wins: {withIt}. Without presence: {withoutIt}.
objectivePresenceWeak.limitation: The sample is small to separate presence from other factors; the position is sampled about once a minute.
objectivePresenceWeak.exercise: Watch two games where the team was at the dragon and check whether vision (ward) arrived first.

leadHeld.title: A lead at 15 minutes usually becomes a win
leadHeld.body: Ahead by +1k or more at 15 min, wins: {withIt}. Behind by −1k or more.
leadHeld.limitation: Gold measures material advantage, not decision quality; the sample is the games with a timeline.
leadHeld.exercise: Keep a replay of a game where you led: find the first objective forced without vision.

leadLost.title: Leading at 15 minutes has not been enough
leadLost.body: Ahead by +1k or more at 15 min, wins: {withIt}. Behind by −1k or more.
leadLost.limitation: An association; it can reflect the opponents' level and the composition, not only a decision.
leadLost.exercise: After a won mid-game fight, pick ONE thing: baron with vision, an open tower, or a reset for items.

costlyDeaths.title: Some deaths cost an objective
costlyDeaths.body: Team deaths followed by an enemy objective within 60 s: {value}.
costlyDeaths.limitation: The 60 s window is a heuristic; an objective may fall for another reason.
costlyDeaths.exercise: After a mid/late death, have one player delay the enemy while the rest choose an alternative target.

isolatedDeaths.title: Deaths with no ally nearby
isolatedDeaths.body: Team deaths with no other roster player within 4,000 units: {value}.
isolatedDeaths.limitation: The position comes from ~1 minute frames; "alone" is an approximation.
isolatedDeaths.exercise: On side waves, agree on who backs off first when the enemy leaves the map.

scattered.title: The team spends a lot of time spread out
scattered.body: Moments with every team player within 6,000 units of an ally: {value}.
scattered.limitation: Being together is not playing well together: split lanes are normal in the early game.
scattered.exercise: After 15 min, mark a meeting point before contesting vision.

grouped.title: The team stays together
grouped.body: Moments with every team player within 6,000 units of an ally: {value}.
grouped.limitation: Proximity does not prove coordination; it only shows where the players were.
grouped.exercise: Keep the rule that, after taking an objective, the next one is chosen before the reset.

conversionSlow.title: Kills take a while to become objectives
conversionSlow.body: Median time from a team kill to its next objective, when one came within 45 s: {median}s over {games} of {kills} kills.
conversionSlow.limitation: It measures the conversions that happened; kills with no objective after are not timed.
conversionSlow.exercise: After a kill with a numbers advantage, call the objective out loud with a command ping.

noTimelines.title: No timelines yet
noTimelines.body: Positioning and minute-by-minute gold readings need the timeline collection.
noTimelines.limitation: Without a timeline, the map numbers simply do not exist for this team.
noTimelines.exercise: Run the timeline collection on the next games.

timelineCoverage.title: Part of the games has no timeline
timelineCoverage.body: Only {games} of {total} games have a timeline: the gold and position readings cover just those.
timelineCoverage.limitation: Map and presence metrics are read only in games with a timeline; they are not extrapolated.
timelineCoverage.exercise: Collect the missing timelines before comparing periods.
